parsed.rationale: All four records are unnamed extensions on `URLSession` spread across four distinct packages — `Playlist`, `Core`, `Playback`, and `MusicShareKit` — each in a file with a different purpose (`PlaylistFetcher.swift`, `URLSession+WebSession.swift`, `URLSessionProtocol.swift`, `RequestService.swift`). The cluster carries no `fields_or_signature` data for any member, so there is no evidence of shared method bodies or overlapping API surface. The name collision is purely structural: Swift allows multiple extensions on the same type across modules, and each extension here almost certainly adds domain-specific helpers relevant only to its own package. Without field-level evidence of duplication, consolidation would risk coupling unrelated domain concerns.
